note: Expected outcome per probe. verdict null = the oracle must return NO finding. Bugs prove there are no false negatives; ok/control/chain cases prove there are no false positives. evals/run_eval.py fails if the case ids here and the probes it runs ever drift apart.

OK-3.desc: GET /api/me returns the caller's own row (own canary is not a leak)

OK-1.desc: GET /api/invoices/{id} for an invoice the caller DOES own -> 200

OK-5.desc: GET /api/documents/{id} for a document the caller DOES own -> 200

OK-2.desc: cross-tenant GET /api/documents/{id} -> 403 whose body QUOTES the id and title; a naive detector calls this a leak

CTRL-BUG-4.desc: the control run: step four ALONE, with no invite -> 403. This is what makes BUG-4 meaningful

BUG-1.desc: IDOR: GET /api/invoices/{id} does not check tenant ownership

BUG-2.desc: listing leak: GET /api/invoices returns every tenant's invoices

BUG-3.desc: chat leak: POST /api/chat answers out of another tenant's content, in prose, with no id to match on

CHAIN-4a.desc: compound step 1-2: the inviter shares ONE invoice by email -> benign

CHAIN-4b.desc: compound step 3: the outsider accepts the invite -> benign, and says nothing about the tenant it just joined them to

BUG-4.desc: compound: the same read that was 403 in CTRL-BUG-4 is now 200, because accepting the invite silently granted tenant membership
